geometry.resolution_method: Use the reviewed UNESCO Manwoldae & Kaesong Chomsongdae component point as a royal-capital/navigation proxy for the Goryeo jurisdiction in 956. Manwoldae was the Goryeo royal palace from 919 and Kaesong was the ruling base. The 956 nobi-status record does not state a physical event locus, so the point is not an event locus, practice extent, or prevalence indicator.

geometry_source.title: Historic Monuments and Sites in Kaesong — Maps
geometry_source.license_status: UNESCO site terms; coordinate used as reference

temporal_identity_check.source: National Research Institute of Cultural Heritage / Kaesong heritage knowledge portal
temporal_identity_check.finding: Manwoldae is identified as the Goryeo royal palace site, founded in 919 and used through the dynasty; therefore a 956 capital-context use does not back-project a later-only site.

abstentions: do not assert the 956 order was physically issued at Manwoldae
do not treat a palace point as Goryeo territorial extent
do not infer territorial practice or prevalence from the navigation point

geometry.resolution_method: Use the modern GeoNames Godomè/Godomey populated-place coordinate as a navigation proxy for historical Jakin after specialist place-identity reconciliation. Historical Jakin is explicitly identified as Jakin [Godomey] by Robin Law and as Jaquin/Jakri/Godomey/Jakin by the Atlas of Mutual Heritage. The point is not the unidentified royal camp, a historical port polygon, or Dahomey practice extent.

historical_identity_source.claim_fitness: Supports historical Jakin↔Godomey identity and transaction-node geography only; not slavery prevalence.

corroborating_identity_source.title: Jaquim
corroborating_identity_source.finding: Historical titles explicitly list Jaquin, Jakri, Godomey and Jakin.

locus_link.notes: The accepted 1727 claim explicitly includes enslaved people supplied for sale to Snelgrave at Jakin. This link locates that named transaction node only; the royal camp remains unresolved.

abstentions: do not replace the existing unresolved Dahomey target geometry
do not treat modern Godomey boundaries as historical Jakin extent
do not use this point for the unidentified royal camp
do not infer Dahomey-wide practice from the transaction node
